articles.title: The Coordination Burden and Cost Challenges of Cell and Gene Therapy Access
articles.summary: As ultra-expensive cell and gene therapies enter the market, self-funded employers face severe administrative and financial complexities in managing coverage and coordination of care. Plan sponsors must navigate intense logistical burdens and reinsurance strategies to handle these multi-million-dollar therapies without destabilizing their health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Fri, 16 Oct 2026 17:59:49 GMT

articles.title: 340B Rebate Restrictions Threaten Hospital Finances Amid Manufacturer Pushback
articles.summary: Ongoing disputes between pharmaceutical manufacturers and hospitals over 340B contract pharmacy restrictions are increasingly impacting hospital cash flow. For self-funded employers and PBMs, these shifting 340B dynamics ripple through the healthcare supply chain, altering drug acquisition costs and impacting overall commercial healthcare trend stability.
articles.source_line: Source: HealthLeaders Media; Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:08:04 GMT

articles.title: PBM Reform Impacts on Supportive Care and Specialty Drug Access
articles.summary: Nicolas Ferreyros discusses how ongoing PBM reform legislative efforts intersect with the clinical and supportive care needs of complex patients. For self-funded employers, shifting regulatory landscapes around PBM practices directly impact specialty drug management, patient out-of-pocket costs, and overall plan design strategies.
articles.source_line: Source: The American Journal of Managed Care; Fri, 16 Oct 2026 19:24:26 GMT
articles.source_name: The American Journal of Managed Care

articles.title: Rethinking GLP-1 Coverage Strategies for Employer Health Plans
articles.summary: The article discusses strategic approaches health plans and employers must consider regarding GLP-1 coverage amid skyrocketing costs and surging demand. For self-funded employers, optimizing benefit design around anti-obesity medications is a critical priority for managing specialty drug spend without sacrificing employee attraction and retention. This directly impacts PBM utilization management strategies like prior authorization and lifestyle management integrations.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Economics; Fri, 16 Oct 2026 18:10:01 GMT

articles.title: Regulatory Barriers Slow Biosimilar Adoption for Self-Funded Plans
articles.summary: Outdated regulatory frameworks are failing to keep pace with scientific advancements in biosimilars, hindering broader market uptake and potential cost savings. For self-funded employers and PBMs, these regulatory bottlenecks delay access to lower-cost biologic alternatives, impacting specialty drug spend management. Streamlining these pathways is critical to unlocking greater value and reducing pharmacy benefit costs.

articles.title: Major Employer Expands Coverage for Obesity Medications
articles.summary: The largest private employer in the U.S. is now offering free weight-loss drugs to its employees, signaling a major shift in corporate wellness benefits. This move intensifies employer pressure around GLP-1 coverage decisions, cost management, and pharmacy benefit plan design. Self-funded employers will need to weigh the high upfront drug spend against long-term health outcomes and talent retention.

articles.title: Rising GLP-1 Costs Drive Pharmacy Strategy Urgency for Self-Funded Staffing Firms
articles.summary: Staffing industry employers are facing intense cost pressures from escalating GLP-1 utilization, forcing a strategic reassessment of their pharmacy benefit management. Self-funded plans in high-turnover industries must adopt targeted utilization management and robust formulary controls to mitigate these unsustainable specialty drug expenses. The trend highlights the critical need for specialized pharmacy strategies to protect employer health plan financial stability.
articles.source_line: Source: Staffing Industry Analysts; Fri, 16 Oct 2026 21:41:39 GMT
